_comment: Known defects on current code, per profile. A fault or invariant
listed here is expected to fail; the run reports it as XFAIL and
stays green. If it starts passing the run reports XPASS and FAILS,
so the entry is removed and the issue closed. Every entry must name
the issue that tracks the defect. Optional max_recovery_seconds and
max_stall_seconds override the default bounds for a fault.
Profiles differ in window length, so a defect that trips the stall
bound in a 60s window (pr, nightly) may not in a 20s one (smoke).

sigul-server: no zombie processes.issue: gpg helper processes spawned during signing are orphaned to PID 1, which never reaps them; ~10 zombies per signing request - issue to be filed

client_connect_and_hang.issue: bridge blocks in force_handshake() with no deadline; one silent TCP connection stops all signing for as long as it stays open (measured: 0 requests served in 60s) - issue to be filed

client_handshake_then_hang.issue: an authenticated client frozen mid-upload holds the bridge's single slot indefinitely; no read deadline on the bridge or server side (measured: 0 requests served in 60s) - issue to be filed

client_backlog_flood.issue: listen backlog of 5 on the client port, drained only between server pairings; 20 idle connections stall the service and the poisoned backlog takes ~25s to drain afterwards - issue to be filed

sigul-server: no zombie processes.issue: gpg helper processes spawned during signing are orphaned to PID 1, which never reaps them; ~10 zombies per signing request (measured: 7423 after 28 min), bounded only by the pod pids limit of ~12k - issue to be filed

sigul-server: RSS growth < 40 MB.issue: kernel task structures for the zombies above are charged to the container (measured: +53 MB over 28 min, ~7 KB per zombie); expected to clear with the zombie fix

client_slow_loris.issue: no per-read deadline on the bridge's client handshake; unverified until the first nightly run

client_half_close_hang.issue: half-closed client holds the slot; unverified until the first nightly run

client_stop_mid_sign.issue: as client_handshake_then_hang, with the client resumed afterwards
